<!--
This template is for bug reports. If you are reporting a bug, please continue on. If you are here for another reason, please see below:

1. To propose a new rule: http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules

3. If you have any questions, please stop by our chatroom: https://gitter.im/eslint/eslint

Note that leaving sections blank will make it difficult for us to troubleshoot and we may have to close the issue.
-->

**Tell us about your environment**
- **ESLint Version:** v3.9.0
- **Node Version:** v7.0.0-pre
- **npm Version:** 3.10.8

**What parser (default, Babel-ESLint, etc.) are you using?** default

**Please show your full configuration:**

<!-- Paste your configuration below: -->

```
{
    "rules": {
        "indent": [
            "error",
            4
        ]
    }
}
```

**What did you do? Please include the actual source code causing the issue.**

<!-- Paste the source code below: -->

``` js
var array = [1,
             2,
             3];
```

**What did you expect to happen?**

This was considered valid before this release. It would be great to have the `first` option for arrays too.

**What actually happened? Please include the actual, raw output from ESLint.**

```
2:14  error  Expected indentation of 4 spaces but found 13  indent
3:14  error  Expected indentation of 4 spaces but found 13  indent
```

<!--
    The following is required for all pull requests:
-->

**What changes did you make? (Give an overview)**

This fixes an issue where array indentation was calculated incorrectly for MemberExpression nodes.

It does this by removing some outdated logic from the `checkIndentInArrayOrObjectBlock` function. As far as I can tell, this logic is no longer necessary because `indent` no longer has a special case for nested arrays.

**Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?**

We should verify that this removed logic wasn't doing something else that I'm unaware of. It passes all the tests and doesn't appear to be necessary anymore, but it would be good to have confirmation of its original purpose. (It looks like it was introduced in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/commit/b11c3c491ae54858e67b23c2129caacae73f8527) /cc @gyandeeps @BYK

issue.body:
and make `master` pass again.

Looks like eslint merged a few changes to the `indent` rule in the [`3.9.x`](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) series, which made `npm run lint` fail for a handful of our files. Luckily, `eslint --fix .` was able to fix all the issues.
